about: Demos that belong at a time of day rather than in the running order.
The rotation answers 'what is next'. This answers 'what is at 9:25', and
they are different questions. When a cue comes due the scheduler pins the
entry it names onto the next slot, lets it play for its own length, and
then does nothing: the rotation's offset was never touched, so every
index after the cue maps exactly where it did and the running order is
not left rotated by one for the rest of the day. The cue does take that
one slot -- whatever the rotation held there waits until the next time
round.
The entry a cue names is usually switched off in the rotation. That is
the normal case rather than an odd one: a demo that is only right at a
particular minute should not come up at random, and a cue can reach a
disabled entry where the panel's jump button cannot.
Copy this to rotation-cues.json to use it. Nothing here is required --
with no cue file the scheduler is exactly the carousel it always was.
name      an entry in the rotation. A name this wall has not got is
skipped with a line, so one cue file is safe across walls.
at        local times, HH:MM, as many as you like.
days      '*', or a list like ['mon','tue'].
seconds   the slot the cue wants. 0 means the entry's own length.
punctual  true cuts the current effect short so the cue lands on its
minute; false waits for the slot boundary, up to a segment
late, and never truncates anything.
window    how late the cue may still fire, in seconds. A wall that was
rebooting at 9:25 plays it at 9:27; one that was off all
morning does not ambush somebody with it at noon.
